levy1895.title: Quelques considérations sur la construction des grands barrages
levy1895.container: Comptes rendus hebdomadaires des séances de l'Académie des sciences 121(6): 288–300 (séance du 5 août 1895)
levy1895.note: p. 288: the danger peculiar to high dams is the uplift ('sous-pression ou pression ascendante') of water that gets into the masonry through cracks over a large enough extent; compared to a boiler without a safety valve; a guard wall with wells, drained by a collector whose flow would warn of trouble (pp. 288–289). p. 289: the usual condition, that horizontal joints do not tend to open at their upstream ends, amounts to keeping the line of pressures in the middle third; it is not enough, and the pressure at the upstream end of every joint must exceed the reservoir's water pressure there. Read in the séance of 5 August 1895.

usbr1998-dso9805.authors: Anderson, C., Mohorovic, C., Mogck, L., Cohen, B., Scott, G.
usbr1998-dso9805.title: Concrete Dams: Case Histories of Failures and Nonfailures with Back Calculations
usbr1998-dso9805.container: Report DSO-98-05. Denver: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Dam Safety Office, December 1998
usbr1998-dso9805.note: Bouzey, pp. 16–22: 22 m masonry gravity dam on horizontally bedded sandstone; 14 March 1884, at el. 368.8 m (crest 371.95 m), 135 m of dam moved downstream up to 0.34 m, shearing the cutoff key, seepage 230 L/s; buttress 1888–89; 27 April 1895, reservoir at el. 371.4 m, upper central part about 10.5 m high and 170 m long swept away, the break nearly level for about 3.5 m from the upstream face then dipping downstream; 'more than 100' deaths (p. 17). Back-calculation at the 1895 break (Fig. BF-4): resultant 4.65 ft from the centre of a 16.24 ft joint without uplift (middle third ±2.71 ft); heel tension about 0.23 MPa with linear uplift (p. 17). Section after ICOLD (1974), Fig. BF-1.

bordes2010.title: Les barrages en France du XVIIIe à la fin du XXe siècle : histoire, évolution technique et transmission du savoir
bordes2010.note: p. 76: the Bouzey failure of 1895 killed 87 people. p. 77, Table 1: Bouzey, 1881, 22 m, reservoir 7.1 million m³. p. 104: built to feed the Canal de l'Est; the 1884 foundation accident and its repair, in which a drainage gallery was proposed and set aside; the 1895 break through the body of the dam ('On déplora 70 morts'); the thin profile and tension at the upstream face; Lévy's note; the ministerial decision of 10 March 1896 to check every existing masonry dam.

ferc2016-ch3.title: Engineering Guidelines for the Evaluation of Hydropower Projects, Chapter III: Gravity Dams
ferc2016-ch3.container: Washington, D.C.: FERC, Division of Dam Safety and Inspections, 4 March 2016
ferc2016-ch3.note: p. 3-27: the table of alternate minimum factors of safety for use with a no-cohesion assumption (Table 2A): 1.5 for the worst static case, 1.3 for the probable maximum flood and after an earthquake. §3-2.4.3.2: grouting alone does not justify assuming an uplift reduction; drains downstream of the curtain, with monitoring to detect a fall in drain efficiency from clogging. Appendix C, Example gravity analysis: φ = 45°, drain effectiveness 50%.

campbell2022.authors: Campbell, R., Rivett, P., Walpole, B.
campbell2022.title: Cleaning of foundation relief drains in concrete dams: a case study of Mahinerangi Dam
campbell2022.container: Australian National Committee on Large Dams (ANCOLD), paper
campbell2022.note: The paper's abstract on the ANCOLD site: 'Non-functioning relief drains, usually, have become plugged with calcium deposits, sediment, or biological growth'; blocked drains raise the uplift beneath a dam. Case study of Mahinerangi Dam, New Zealand.

bchydro-sitec2021.title: Site C Clean Energy Project: Geotechnical Safety Overview Report
bchydro-sitec2021.note: p. 2: the two-part remedy identified in fall 2020. p. 3: the shale bedrock and its bedding planes; in 1978 a concrete gravity dam was judged not feasible on the foundation bedrock, and the design was an earthfill dam. p. 4: the right-bank roller-compacted concrete buttress and its shear key; small movements in 2018 on a deeper bedding plane. p. 6: up to 125 piles up to 2.5 m across through the deeper plane, and more drainage. Appendix A (Technical Advisory Board summary statement), p. 3: movements of about 5 mm at El. 372 m; p. 4: the contingency case adopted 16° and the plane mobilized about 11°.
